topic.title: Pop Culture Quiz by Calm Your Wits Quizzing

events.description:
Is your Instagram screentime begging for overtime pay? Are your friendships tested every time there is a Marvel vs DC debate?

If you are someone who knows the next brainrot song before it goes viral, join us to test your pop culture knowledge and stand a chance to win bragging rights and prizes!

The quiz will cover sitcoms, memes, entertainment, music, anime, and overall internet & pop culture. If you have never attended a quiz before, this is a great place to start. Every question is framed in a way that will let you work out the answer, and we are liberal with hints.

About Calm Your Wits:

Calm Your Wits Quizzing is a Bengaluru-based quizzing collective that curates and hosts engaging, beginner-friendly pub quizzes across India. Founded by quizmaster Sanket Mandal, they have expanded beyond the Bengaluru quizzing circuit to host regular events in Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, and Hyderabad. Launched with the intention of avoiding the intimidating archetype of traditional academic trivia, their style leans towards long-form questions, with lots of clues and audio-visual elements thrown in to help participants arrive at the answer. Quizmaster Sanket also draws heavily from humour on social media, cleverly using tweets, Instagram reels, and memes to make questions on even the most serious of topics. It’s a way of reminding people that all that doomscrolling can actually come in handy, and that knowledge can come from anywhere if we’re open to the possibilities. Expect questions that keep you guessing, hints that reward lateral thinking, and a few intentional misdirects that may have you arguing with your teammates. Come early, and come curious.

You can follow them on Instagram 
@calm.your.wits.quizzing

topic.title: Folding Ninjas - Origami Club with Roligami

events.description:
Not every gathering needs to be a formal workshop! Our Casual Fold & Connect Nights are all about relaxed creativity, sharing, and building community through Origami. Whether you’re seeking a new hobby, a meditative practice, or a creative outlet, the Folding Ninjas welcomes you! No prior experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and enthusiasm.

Absolute Beginners: We’ll help you get started with some easy folds!

Intermediate Folders: Opportunity to refine techniques and learn and seek help from fellow folders

Advanced Practitioners: Space to experiment, teach others, and push creative boundaries

Meet-Up Structure

Welcome and Warm-Up (30 minutes)

Check-In: Grab your name tag and settle in

Ice-Breaker Activity: A quick origami-related game or quick fold to get everyone engaged

Skill Level Check-In: Beginners are paired with experienced folders for personalized guidance

Free-Form Folding (120 minutes)

No Structured Instructions but beginners will be provided with guidance

Bring your own projects or start something new

Collaborative and spontaneous folding

Free exchange of techniques and ideas

Show and Share (30 minutes)

Members showcase their completed projects

Constructive feedback and celebration of individual achievements

Informal networking and social time

What to Bring

Beginners: Nothing! We provide all materials

Experienced Folders:

Your own specialty papers (optional)

Any unique tools or templates you’d like to share

Completed projects for show and tell

Snacks to share (optional)

Materials Provided

Variety of origami papers

Instructional guides

Basic tools (rulers, pencil, paper cutter, glue)

Who is Roligami?

Roli Agrawal, fondly known as 
roligami
, is a multi-disciplinary designer and passionate craft enthusiast. Inspired by her love for Japanese culture, she has been exploring and teaching origami for over a decade. Roli’s workshops are a celebration of creativity, and her delightful creations are showcased on Instagram 
@roligami
.

Join us and add a handmade touch to your holiday cheer!

Agenda

This will be a discussion focused session.

In a previous IWCB session, we talked about the journey of a blog post from idea to publication. In this session, we want to talk about the life of a blog post 
after
 you publish it.

Do you edit your blog posts after you’ve published them? What kinds of edits do you allow yourself to make? Would you ever consider deleting a piece of writing you’ve already published?

Do you share your blog posts with your friends? What about the communities you’re part of? What drives you to share your writing in this way?

What are your feelings about likes, shares, analytics, or other engagement metrics on your writing? Do you like to track such metrics?

Do you ever go back to read your old blog posts? Why or why not?

Have you ever thought about what you’d like your writing to add up to in the long term? In ten or fifteen years, are you hoping to tell a story, or meander through different ones?

We’ll spend the last hour of the meetup writing and publishing a piece on our personal websites. We’ll provide writing prompts to get you started.

Remember to bring a device you can use to write and post to your blog!

What is IndieWebClub?

IndieWebClub is part of a growing 
world-wide network of meetups
 for everyone who wants to take back their web experience from social media 
silos
, and own their online identities & content, or just want support with blogging!

Want to blog more and looking for: ideas, momentum, and a supportive community?

Join a gathering of like-minded people and get friendly support with writing, creating, and anything related to using and improving your own website!

You 
do not
 need to have any tech background or experience in having your own website. You can even start with a Google Doc or your local notes app!

About IndieWebClub Bangalore

We have a WhatsApp community where we post announcements and share work done by our members. Please join 
by clicking here
.

 for a regularly updated feed of blog posts by our members.
